questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$~be a differentiable function such that $f\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}, f\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = 0$~and $f^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = 1$~and let $g\left(x\right) = {∫}_x^{\pi4}\left(f^{'}\left(t\right)\sec t + \tan t \sec tf\left(t\right)\right)dt$~for~$x \in \left[\dfrac{π}{4}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right) .$~Then $\lim_{x \to  \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) -}g \left($x\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$g\left(x\right) = {∫}_x^{\pi4}\left(f^{'}\left(t\right)\sec t + \tan t \sec tf\left(t\right)\right)dt$

$⇒ g\left(x\right) = {∫}_x^{\pi4}d\left(f\left(t\right) \cdot \sec t\right)⇒ g\left(x\right) = {f\left(t\right)\sec t}_x^{\pi4}$

$g\left(x\right) = f\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)sec\dfrac{π}{4} - f\left(x\right) \cdot \sec x$

$g \left(x\right) = 2 - f \left($x\right)\sec x = 2 - \left(\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{\cos x}\right)

Now taking limit both side, we get

$\lim_{x \to \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) -}g \left($x\right) = 2 - \lim_{x \to \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) -}\left(\dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{\cos x}\right)$

Using L'Hospital Rule

$= 2 - \lim_{x \to \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) -}f^{'} \left(x\right)\left(-$\sin x\right)$

$= 2 + \dfrac{f^{'}\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{π}{2}} =2 + \dfrac{1}{1} =3$

questions.q: The minimum value of the function $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}e\left|x - t\right|dt$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}e\left|x - t\right|dt$

Now For $x \le 0$

$f \left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}e^{t - x}dt = e^{- x}\left(e^{2} - 1\right)$

And for $0 < x < 2$

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}e^{x - t}dt + {∫}_x^{2}e^{t - x}dt = e^{x} + e^{2 - x} - 2$

For $x \ge 2$

$f \left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{2}e^{x - t}dt = e^{x - 2}\left(e^{2} - 1\right)$

Now for $x ≤ 0, f \left(x\right)$ is decreasing as~$e^{- x}$~is decreasing function~and $x ≥ 2, f \left(x\right)$ is increasing as $e^{x - 2}$~is increasing function,

So, minimum value of $f \left($x\right)$ lies in $x \in \left($0, 2\right)$

Applying A.M ≥ G.M in $e^{x} + e^{2 - x}$we get,

\dfrac{e^{x} + e^{2 - x}}{2} \ge \sqrt{e^{x} \times e^{2 - x}}

$⇒ e^{x} + e^{2 - x} ≥ 2e$

Hence, the minimum value of $f \left($x\right)$ is $2e - 2 = 2 \left($e - 1\right)$

questions.q: For $x \in \left(- \dfrac{π}{2}, \dfrac{π}{2}\right), if $y\left($x\right) = ∫ $\dfrac{cosec x + \sin x}{cosec xsecx + \tan x\sin^{2}x}$dx$ and $\lim_{x \to \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) -}y \left($x\right) = 0$ then y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{cosecx + \sin x}{cosecxsecx + \tan x\sin^{2}x}dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\sin x} + \sin x}{\dfrac{1}{\sin x \cos x} + \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\left(\sin^{2}x\right)}dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\dfrac{1 + \sin^{2}x}{\sin x}}{\dfrac{1 + \sin^{4}x}{\sin x \cos x}}dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 + \sin^{2}x\right)\cos x}{1 + \sin^{4}x}dx$

Let, $\sin x = t$

$cosxdx = dt$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + t^{2}}{1 + t^{4}}dt$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{t2}}{t^{2} + \dfrac{1}{t2}}dt$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{t2}}{\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2 + 2}dt$

Let, $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = u$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1}{u^{2} + 2}du$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{u}{2}\right) + C$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{t - \dfrac{1}{t}}{2}\right) + C$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x - \dfrac{1}{\sin x}}{2}\right) + C$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x - cosecx}{2}\right) + C$

Now, $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{π}{2} -}f\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \dfrac{π}{2} -}f\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{π}{2} -}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x - cosecx}{2}\right) + C\right] = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(0\right) + C = 0$

$⇒ C = 0$

$⇒ f \left(x\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x - cosecx}{2}\right)

$⇒ y \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{sin\dfrac{π}{4} - cosec\dfrac{π}{4}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} - \sqrt{2}}{2}\right)

$⇒ y \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{- 1\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ y \left(\dfrac{π}{4}) = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1} $\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2})

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- \log_{\mathrm{e}}2}^{\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}e^{x}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(e^{x} + \sqrt{1 + e^{2x}}\right)\right)dx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $I = {∫}_{- \log_{\mathrm{e}}2}^{\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}e^{x}\left[\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(e^{x} + \sqrt{1 + e^{2x}}\right)\right]dx$

Let us substitute~$e^{x} = t$

$⇒ e^{x}dx = dt$

Lower limit~$= e^{- \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Upper limit~$= e^{\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(2\right)} = 2$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{12}^{2}1 \times \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + t^{2}}\right]dt$

Apply integration by-parts.

$∫ u\left(t\right)v\left(t\right)dt = u\left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt - ∫ \left(u ' \left(t\right) ∫ v\left(t\right)dt\right)dt$

Take~$u\left(t\right) = \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left[t + \sqrt{1 + t^{2}}\right], v\left(t\right) = 1$

$⇒ u ' \left(t\right) = \dfrac{1}{t + \sqrt{1 + t^{2}}}\left(1 + \dfrac{2t}{2\sqrt{1 + t^{2}}}\right) = t$

$= {tln\left(\sqrt{t^{2} + 1} + x\right)}_{12}^{2} - {∫}_{1/2}^{2}\dfrac{t}{t^{2} + 1}dt$

$= {tln\sqrt{t^{2} + 1} + t - \sqrt{t^{2} + 1}}_{12}^{2}$

$= \left[2\ln \left(\sqrt{5} + 2\right) - \sqrt{5}\right] - \left[\dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\right]

=\ln \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} ( 2 + \sqrt{5}{)}^{2}}{1 + \sqrt{5}}) - \dfrac{5}{2}$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $f$~be a real valued continuous function on  \left[0, 1\right]$ and $f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{1}  \left(x - t\right)f \left($t\right)dt$. Then which of the~following points \left($x, y\right)$ lies on the curve~$y = f  \left(x\right)?$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = x\left(1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt\right) - {∫}_{0}^{1}tf \left(t\right)dt$

$f\left(x\right) = Ax - B . . . \left(i\right)$

$A = 1 + {∫}_{0}^{1}f\left(t\right)dt = 1 + {∫}_{0}^{1} \left(At - B\right)dt$

$⇒ A = 2\left(1 - B\right) . . . \left(ii\right)$

Also~$B = {∫}_{0}^{1}tf \left($t\right)dt = {∫}_{0}^{1} \left(At^{2} - Bt\right)dt$

$A = \dfrac{9}{2}B . . . \left(iii\right)$

From~ \left($ii\right), \left($iii\right)$

$A = $\dfrac{18}{13},$B = $\dfrac{4}{13}

So,~$f\left($x\right) = $\dfrac{18}{13}$x - $\dfrac{4}{13}

~$⇒ f\left($6\right) = $\dfrac{18 \times 6 - 4}{13} =$8$

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{96 x^2 \cos ^2 x}{1+e^x} d x \\ & 2 I=2 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 96 x^2 \cos ^2 x d x \\ & I=96 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} x^2 \cos ^2 x d x \\ & =48 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} x^2(1+\cos 2 x) d x \\ & =2 \pi^2+48(0-0)-48 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} x \sin 2 x d x \\ & =2 \pi^2-12 \pi+[0-0]=\pi\left(2 \pi^2-12\right) \\ & =\pi\left(\alpha \pi^2+\beta\right) \\ & \Rightarrow(\alpha+\beta)^2=100\end{aligned}$

$& Newton -& Leibnitz rule&

$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left({∫}_{f\left(x\right)}^{g\left(x\right)}h \left(x\right) d x\right) = g ' \left($x\right)h\left(g ( x )\right) - f ' \left(x\right)h\left(f ( x )\right)$

Given that

${∫}_{0}^{x}\sqrt{1 - \left(f^{'} ( t )\right)2}dt = {∫}_{0}^{x}f ( t ) dt$

Differentiate~$w . r . t . x$

\sqrt{1 - \left(f^{'} ( x )\right)2} =$f ( x )$

Squaring on both sides
$⇒ 1 - \left(f^{'} ( x )\right)2 = ( f ( x ) {)}^{2}$

$⇒ \left(f^{'} ( x )\right)2 = 1 - ( f ( x ) {)}^{2}$

f \left($x\right) = y ⇒ f ' \left($x\right) = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$
$⇒ $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx})2 = 1 - y^{2} ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \pm \sqrt{1 - y^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{1 - y^{2}} = \pmdx$

By using Variable Separable form

$\sin^{- 1}y = $\pm$x + c$

When~$x = 0, y = 0 ⇒ c = 0 .$

$∴ \sin^{- 1}y = x ⇒ y = \sin x$

Now $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1}{x2}{∫}_{0}^{x}$sintdt$

It is in the form of~$\dfrac{0}{0}$~so apply L hospital's rule

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[{∫}_{0}^{x}$sintdt\right]}{\dfrac{d \left(x^{2}\right)}{d x}}

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$

f\left($x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\sin x \cos y\left($y + ksiny\right)dy$

f\left($x\right) = x + \sin x{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}ycosydy + \dfrac{k}{2}\sin x{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\sin 2ydy$

f\left($x\right) = x + $\sin x\left[$y{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}cosydy - {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\left\{\dfrac{d}{dy}y{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}cosydy\right\}dy\right] + \dfrac{k}{2}\sin x{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\sin 2ydy$

$f \left($x\right) = x + \sin x $\left[\dfrac{π}{2} -$1] + $\dfrac{k}{2}$\sin x \times \left(1\right)$

$f \left($x\right) = x + $\dfrac{( \pi - 2 ) \sin x}{2} + \dfrac{ksinx}{2} . . . \left($iii\right)$

from~$( i )$~and~$( iii )$

$k = $\dfrac{π}{2} -$1 + $\dfrac{k}{2}

$k = $\pi -$2$

Hence, $f ( x ) = x + ( $\pi -$2 ) \sin x$

questions.q: If ${∫}_{0}^{3}\dfrac{15x^{3}}{1 + x^{2} + \sqrt{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)3}}dx = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}$, where $\alpha, \beta$ are integers, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{3}\dfrac{15x^{3}}{1 + x^{2} + \sqrt{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)3}}dx = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}$,~

Taking L.H.S we get~${∫}_{0}^{3}\dfrac{15x^{3}}{1 + x^{2} + \sqrt{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)3}}dx$

Now put~$1 + x^{2} = t^{2}$

$⇒ 2xdx = 2tdt$

$⇒ xdt = tdt$

$∴ {∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{15\left(t^{2} - 1\right)tdt}{t^{2} + t^{3}}$

$= 15{∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{t\left(t^{2} - 1\right)}{t\sqrt{1 + t}}dt$

Now put~$1 + t = u^{2}⇒ dt = 2udu$

So, the integral will be~$15{∫}_{2}^{3}\dfrac{\left(u^{2} - 1\right)2 - 1}{u} \times 2udu$

$= 30{∫}_{2}^{3}\left(u^{4} - 2u^{2}\right)du$

$= 30{\dfrac{u5}{5} - \dfrac{2u^{3}}{3}}_{2}^{3}$

$= 30 \left[\dfrac{1}{5} \left({3}^{5} - {2}^{5}\right) - \dfrac{2}{3}\left({3}^{3} - {2}^{3}\right)\right]

$= 30 \left[\dfrac{1}{5} \lleft(9\sqrt{3} --4\sqrt{2}\right) - \dfrac{2}{3}\llleft(3\sqrt{3} --2\sqrt{2})]$

$= 30 \left[- $\dfrac{1}{5} \times \sqrt{3} + \dfrac{8}{15}\sqrt{2}\right]

$= - $6\sqrt{3} ++16\sqrt{2}$

So,~${∫}_{0}^{4}\dfrac{15x^{3}}{1 + x^{2} + \sqrt{\left(1 + x^{2}\right)3}}dx = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}

$⇒ - $6\sqrt{3} ++16\sqrt{2} = \alpha\sqrt{2} + \beta\sqrt{3}$

Now on comparing we get,~$\alpha =16, \beta = -6$

$∴ \alpha + \beta =10

$

questions.q: \left|\dfrac{120}{\pi3}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{x^{2}\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx\right|$ is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{x^{2}\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

Now using the property ${∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right) d x = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right) d x + {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(2a - x\right) d x$ we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}\left(x^{2} - \left(\pi - x\right)2\right) d x$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}\left(2\pi x - {π}^{2}\right) d x$

$⇒ I = 2\pi\mathop{{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{x \cdot \sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x ⏟}_{I1} - {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x} d x$

Now, solving ${I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{x \cdot \sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}dx . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{ \left(\dfrac{π}{2} -x\right)\cdot\text{ \sin x \cos x }}${\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$dx . . . . \left(2\right)$

Adding both equations we get,

$⇒ 2{I}_{1} = $\dfrac{π}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = $\dfrac{π}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$dx$

Now, putting the value in $I$ we get,

$⇒ I = 2\pi \cdot $\dfrac{π}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{x \cdot \sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$dx - {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$d x$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$d x$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin x \cos x}{1 - 2\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x}$d x$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{2}2x}$d x$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin 2x}{2 - \sin^{2}2x}$d x$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{2}{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sin 2x}{1 + \cos^{2}2x}$d x$

Now, let $\cos 2x = t ⇒ - 2\sin 2xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{2}{∫}_{1}^{- 1}\dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 + t^{2}}$d t$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{4}{∫}_{- 1}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1 + t^{2}}$d t$

$⇒ I = - $\dfrac{\pi2}{4} \cdot \dfrac{π}{2} = - \dfrac{\pi3}{8}

Hence, \dfrac{120}{\pi3}\left|{∫}_{0}^{π}\dfrac{x^{2}\sin x \cos x}{\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x}$d x\right| = $\dfrac{120}{\pi3} \times \dfrac{\pi3}{8} =$15$

$

questions.q: Let ${I}_{n} = {∫}_{1}^{e}x^{19} ( log | x | {)}^{n}dx,$ where $n \in N$. If \left(20\right){I}_{10} = \alpha{I}_{9} + \beta{I}_{8},$~for natural numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$, then $\alpha - \beta$ equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& ${I}_{n} = {∫}_{1}^{e}x^{19} ( log | x | {)}^{n}dx, n \in N$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = {∫}_{1}^{e}x^{19}\left(\log x\right)ndx, ∵$~for~$1 0$

Integrating by using by parts rule,~${∫}_a^{b}\left(u \cdot v\right)dx = {u ∫ vdx}_a^{b} - {∫}_a^{b}\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\right) ∫ vdx\right]dx,$~taking~$u = \log x \text{ and } v = x^{19},$~we get

${I}_{n} = {\left(\log x\right)n ∫ x^{19}dx}_{1}^{e} - {∫}_{1}^{e}\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log x\right)n ∫ x^{19}dx\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = {\left(\log x\right)n\left(\dfrac{x20}{20}\right)}_{1}^{e} - {∫}_{1}^{e}\left[n\left(\log x\right)n - 1 \times \dfrac{1}{x} \times \left(\dfrac{x20}{20}\right)\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = \left[\left(loge\right)n\left(\dfrac{e20}{20}\right) - 0\right] - {∫}_{1}^{e}\left[n\left(\log x\right)n - 1 \times \left(\dfrac{x19}{20}\right)\right]dx$

$⇒ {I}_{n} = \left(\dfrac{e20}{20}\right) - \dfrac{n}{20}{∫}_{1}^{e}x^{19}\left(\log x\right)n - 1dx$

$⇒ 20{I}_{n} = e^{20} - n{I}_{n - 1}$

Hence, we get~$20{I}_{10} = e^{20} - 10{I}_{9} . . . \left(i\right)$~and

$20{I}_{9} = e^{20} - 9{I}_{8} . . . \left(ii\right)$

On subtracting the above two equations, we get

$20{I}_{10} - 20{I}_{9} = - 10{I}_{9} + 9{I}_{8}$

$⇒ 20{I}_{10} = 10{I}_{9} + 9{I}_{8}$

Given~$20{I}_{10} = \alpha{I}_{9} + \beta{I}_{8}$

$⇒ \alpha =10, \beta =9$~and hence~$\alpha - \beta =1 .$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

& $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{\left(1 + x^{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}, x \in \mathbb{R} - \left\{- 1\right\}, n \in \mathbb{N}, n > 2$,

$f^{n} \left(x\right) = ( fofof . . . .$~upto~$n$~times)~\left(x\right)$,

Now finding~f\l$left(f\left($x\right)) = \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{\left[1 + \left(f\left(x\right)\right)n\right]\dfrac{1}{n}}$

$⇒ $f\lleft(f\left(x\right)) = $\dfrac{x\left(1 + x^{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{x}{\left(1 + x^{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}\right)n\right]\dfrac{1}{n}}

$⇒ $f\l$left(f\left($x\right)) = \dfrac{x}{\left[1 + 2x^{n}\right]\dfrac{1}{n}}$

Similarly,~f^{n}\left($x\right) = \dfrac{x}{\left(1 + nx^{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}$

Now solving the integral we get,

$I = {∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{xn - 1}{\left(1 + nx^{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}$dx$

Now let,~$1 + nx^{n} = t^{n}$

$⇒ n^{2}x^{n - 1}dx = nt^{n - 1}dt$

$I = {∫}_{1}^{\left(1 + n\right)\$\text{ ddfrac }{1}{n}}$\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{n}t^{n - 1}dt}{t}

$⇒ I = ${\dfrac{1}{n}\dfrac{tn - 1}{n - 11}}_{1}^{\left(1 + n\right)\dfrac{1}{n}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{n \left($n - 1\right)}\left(\left(1 + n\right)1 - $\dfrac{1}{n} -$1\right)$

Now solving the limit we get,

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left(1 + n\right)1 - \dfrac{1}{n} -1}${n\left(n - 1\right)}$

Now let~$n = $\dfrac{1}{h}~so the limit changes to,

$\lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{ \left($1 + $\dfrac{1}{h}\right)$1 - h - $1}{\dfrac{1}{h}\left(\dfrac{1}{h} -$1\right)}$

$= \lim_{h \to $0}\dfrac{\left($1 + $\dfrac{1}{h}\left($1 - h\right)\right) - $1}{\dfrac{1}{h}\left(\dfrac{1}{h} -$1\right)}$

$= \lim_{h \to 0} \left(1 - h\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{h} -1\right)$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}h \left($1 - h\right)\left($1 - h\right)$

$= \lim_{h \to 0}h = 0$

$

questions.q: Let (f:(0, $\infty) \rightarrow \mathbf{R}$) be a twice differentiable function. If for some ($\mathrm{a} \neq$0, \int_0^1 f(\lambda x) $\mathrm{d} \lambda=\mathrm{a}$f(x), f(1)=1) and (f(16)=$\frac{1}{8}$), then (16-f^{\prime}  \left(\frac{1}{16}\right)$) is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, $\int_0^1 f(\lambda x) d \lambda=a f(x)$
Let $\lambda x=ud \lambda=\frac{1}{x} d u\therefore$ From (1) $\frac{1}{x} \int_0^x f(u) d u=a f(x)\Rightarrow \int_0^x f(u) d u=\operatorname{axf}(x)$
Differentiate both sides
$\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=a\left(x f^{\prime}(x)+f(x)\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad f(x)=a x f^{\prime}(x)+a f(x) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(1-a) f(x)=a x f^{\prime}(x) \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)}=\frac{(1-a)}{a} \cdot \frac{1}{x}
\end{aligned}$
Integrate both side w.r.t. ( $x$ )
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{f(x)} d x=\frac{(1-a)}{a} \int \frac{1}{x} d x \\
& \Rightarrow \ln f(x)=\left(\frac{1-a}{a}\right) \ln x+c
\end{aligned}$
Now at $x=1 f(1)=1\Rightarrow c=0$
Also given $f(16)=\frac{1}{8}$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad \frac{1}{8}=(16)^{\frac{1-a}{a}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2^{-3}=2^{\frac{4-4 a}{a}} \\
& \Rightarrow \quad-3=\frac{4-4 a}{a} \\
& \Rightarrow-3 a=4-4 a \\
& \Rightarrow a=4 \\
& \therefore \quad f(x)=x^{-3 / 4} \\
& f(x)=\frac{-3}{4} x^{-\frac{7}{4}}
\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \text { Put } x=\frac{1}{16} \\ & f^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)=\frac{-3}{4}\left(\frac{1}{16}\right)^{-7 / 4}=\frac{-3}{4} \cdot 2^{-4 x\left(\frac{-7}{4}\right)}=-96 \\ & \therefore \quad 16-f^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{16}\right) \Rightarrow 16-(-96)=112\end{aligned}$
